interest: Illuminates fierce debates between MacArthur, Washington, and Japanese officials over police decentralization versus Cold War internal security needs.
overview: This file documents the reorganization, decentralization, and contentious governance of the Japanese police system under Allied occupation between 1947 and 1949. Originating from the 1947 Police Law, the records detail the creation of municipal police forces, the National Rural Police, and civilian public safety commissions under Prime Minister Tetsu Katayama and General Douglas MacArthur. The documents trace severe administrative and operational challenges—including acute municipal funding shortages, equipment deficiencies, and communist-led labor unrest—and capture the escalating struggle between Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida, the U.S. State Department, the Department of the Army, and SCAP over police recentralization and the implementation of NSC 13/2 and NSC 13/3.
